summary: Freeze the remaining Issue #67 performance contracts after Issue #88 already bounded Python traversal: async Host checkpoint/durable commit barriers, reuse of chunk-assembled bytes instead of immediate synchronous reread, and content-hash durable dedup, plus a repeatable benchmark harness.

pointers: identical durable generation is not rewritten
eval waits for restorable durable commit

steps: Re-read Issue #67 and its latest comment: commit 91f70de/Issue #88 already solved the unbounded traversal/context preflight portion, so this candidate does not reopen that work.

Audited current protocol-v5 runtime: chunked onResult still synchronously writes/renames the host snapshot; runEntry synchronously rereads it and publishDurable synchronously open/write/fsync/renames every generation.

Added a real dedup regression using nanosecond mtime identity, a restorable-before-settle commit barrier regression, and a structural guard that will remain RED until the hot path uses awaited fs/promises and reuses an assembled checkpoint payload.
Added a non-gating benchmark command that exercises 0.5/2/6 MiB supported state in ephemeral/durable modes and reports p50/p95 latency, event-loop p95, peak heap and final durable-root bytes.

evidence.note: The remaining redundant synchronous Host I/O and repeated durable rewrite are still present; Python traversal budget is already fixed and excluded from this patch.
Production patch intentionally not applied yet; GitHub Actions will capture RED/GREEN once the branch PR is opened.

limitations: The benchmark is observational and intentionally has no CI performance threshold because shared GitHub runners are noisy.
Startup durable-root rescan and explicit reset cleanup are not the repeated per-cell hot path and remain synchronous unless later measurements justify changing them.
